nodes.label: Investigation, Arrest, Search and Detention
nodes.summary: Police and ICAC investigatory powers, arrest (with/without warrant), search, seizure, detention, and police bail.

nodes.label: Source of Investigatory Power
nodes.summary: Police Force Ordinance (Cap 232) ss.50, 50A, 51, 52, 54; ICAC Ordinance (Cap 204) ss.10, 10A. Common law powers preserved (e.g. entry to prevent breach of peace).

nodes.label: Police Force Ordinance (Cap 232) s.50
nodes.summary: Police powers of arrest, entry and search.

nodes.label: Police Force Ordinance (Cap 232) s.50A
nodes.summary: Search of persons arrested.

nodes.label: Police Force Ordinance (Cap 232) s.51
nodes.summary: Power to take finger impressions and photographs.

nodes.label: Police Force Ordinance (Cap 232) s.52
nodes.summary: Detention after arrest; person must be brought before magistrate as soon as practicable.

nodes.label: Police Force Ordinance (Cap 232) s.54
nodes.summary: Search warrant issued by magistrate.

nodes.label: ICAC Ordinance (Cap 204) s.10
nodes.summary: ICAC powers of arrest without warrant.

nodes.label: ICAC Ordinance (Cap 204) s.10A
nodes.summary: ICAC detention and bail powers.

nodes.label: Archer v Commissioner of Police of the Metropolis (comparative)
nodes.summary: Protective detention in narrow circumstances. Comparative authority.

nodes.label: Reasonable Suspicion / Reasonable Belief
nodes.summary: Reasonable suspicion = honest suspicion based on facts that would objectively cause suspicion; lower standard than belief. Reasonable belief required for some powers (e.g. s.54 search warrant). Factors: source/quality of information, urgency, suspect's conduct, prior history.

nodes.label: Zenuni v R (PC) (comparative)
nodes.summary: Reasonable suspicion standard. Persuasive authority in HK.

nodes.label: Arrest With Warrant
nodes.summary: Warrant issued by magistrate under Cap 227 s.31 or Cap 221 s.71. Information must be on oath showing reasonable cause to suspect.

nodes.label: Magistrates Ordinance (Cap 227) s.31
nodes.summary: Warrant for arrest issued by magistrate.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.71
nodes.summary: Warrant for arrest by magistrate.

nodes.label: R v Leach (comparative)
nodes.summary: Informant material may include privileged/sensitive material; PII issues.

nodes.label: Arrest Without Warrant
nodes.summary: Cap 232 s.50(1): 'reasonably suspected of having committed an offence'. Cap 204 s.10(2): ICAC officer may arrest without warrant on reasonable suspicion. Procedure: inform suspect of grounds at time of arrest or as soon as practicable; otherwise arrest unlawful and may affect admissibility of subsequent confession.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Lam Tat Ming (2000) 3 HKCFAR 168
nodes.summary: Effect of failure to inform grounds of arrest. May affect admissibility of subsequent confession.

nodes.label: Use of Force on Arrest
nodes.summary: Force must be reasonable; excessive force may lead to exclusion of evidence or civil liability.

nodes.label: Search With Warrant
nodes.summary: Search warrant issued by magistrate under Cap 232 s.54, Cap 204 s.13, or other specific ordinances. Must specify premises and items sought with sufficient particularity. Journalistic/privileged material: special regime under Cap 1 Pt XII (ss.83-85) requires circuit judge warrant. Legal professional privilege: generally immune from seizure.

nodes.label: ICAC Ordinance (Cap 204) s.13
nodes.summary: ICAC search warrant powers.

nodes.label: Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance (Cap 1) Part XII, ss.83-85
nodes.summary: Special regime for journalistic and privileged material; requires circuit judge warrant.

nodes.label: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police [2020] 2 HKLRD 1289
nodes.summary: Search of journalistic material; NSL Implementation Rules vs ordinary regime.

nodes.label: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police (No 2)
nodes.summary: Appeal development on journalistic material search.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Lai Man Ling [2021] HKCFA 28
nodes.summary: NSL evidence-gathering powers; time limits on substantive offence do not apply to conspiracy.

nodes.label: Search Without Warrant
nodes.summary: Limited powers: entry to premises where arrestable offence has been committed (Cap 232 s.50(3)), search of person arrested (s.50A). Must be reasonably necessary; search of person must be done by person of same sex.

nodes.label: Seizure of Property / Documents / Digital Material
nodes.summary: Police may seize anything which may be evidence of an offence. Digital devices: powers under Cap 232 s.54A, subject to privacy concerns and proportionality. NSL: Implementation Rules provide for broader seizure powers in national security cases. Return of property: Cap 221 s.102.

nodes.label: Police Force Ordinance (Cap 232) s.54A
nodes.summary: Police powers to search digital devices, subject to privacy and proportionality.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.102
nodes.summary: Return of property; court may order return of stolen property, disposal of exhibits, forfeiture.

nodes.label: Detention After Arrest
nodes.summary: Accused must be brought before magistrate 'as soon as practicable' (Cap 232 s.52). ICAC custody: similar under Cap 204 s.10A(2). Detention beyond 48 hours requires court order (Cap 221 s.12). Right to legal adviser: right to consult solicitor privately; denial may render confession inadmissible.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.12
nodes.summary: Detention beyond 48 hours requires court order.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Leung Kwok Hung [2005] 3 HKLRD 164
nodes.summary: CFA public assembly/proportionality authority. Public paragraph proof is attached for the case identity and constitutional restriction principles; it is not a detention/legal-adviser authority.

nodes.label: Detainee Rights
nodes.summary: Right to inform relative/friend, right to copies of records, right to medical attention.

nodes.label: Release / Charge / Police Bail / ICAC Bail
nodes.summary: After investigation, police must either charge or release, with or without bail. Police bail under Cap 232 s.52(1A) or Cap 221 s.9B; can impose conditions. ICAC bail under Cap 204 s.10A(3).

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.9B
nodes.summary: Police bail powers.

nodes.label: DPP v Richards (comparative)
nodes.summary: Implied condition of surrender for police bail.

nodes.label: Gizzonio v Chief Constable of Derbyshire Constabulary (comparative)
nodes.summary: Police bail decision immunity.

nodes.label: Arrest/Detention Flow: Identify Power
nodes.summary: Step 1: Identify whether power arises under statute (Cap 232/Cap 204) or common law.

nodes.label: Arrest/Detention Flow: Reasonable Suspicion
nodes.summary: Step 2: Establish reasonable suspicion based on objective facts.

nodes.label: Arrest/Detention Flow: Arrest With/Without Warrant
nodes.summary: Step 3: Execute arrest with or without warrant depending on circumstances and statutory authority.

nodes.label: Arrest/Detention Flow: Inform Grounds
nodes.summary: Step 4: Inform suspect of grounds of arrest at time of arrest or as soon as practicable.

nodes.label: Arrest/Detention Flow: Transport and Detention
nodes.summary: Step 5: Transport to station; detention with access to legal adviser and detainee rights.

nodes.label: Arrest/Detention Flow: Charge, Release or Bail
nodes.summary: Step 6: Charge the accused, release with/without bail, or bring before magistrate.
